_note: Golden in-lesson doubts. LOCAL DB lessons only (ids exist in the local ailernova_aws copy). expectLang follows owner decision 1a (English, except Hindi/Sanskrit lessons). Depth follows 2a (class level wins; book lessons use the book's class).

cases.q: Chlorophyll green kyu dikhta hai?
cases.mustDo: Answer in simple English: chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light and reflects green light, so we see green.
cases.mustNot: Reply in Hinglish or Hindi; say chlorophyll absorbs green light.

cases.q: Dark reaction raat ko hoti hai na?
cases.mustDo: Say clearly NO: it does not need light directly but runs in the daytime using ATP/NADPH from the light reaction.
cases.mustNot: Say it happens at night, or contradict itself.

cases.q: Agar 12 CO2 molecules use hon to kitne glucose molecules banenge?
cases.mustDo: Answer 2 glucose molecules, with the reason 6 CO2 make 1 glucose.
cases.mustNot: Give any other number.

cases.q: How many grams of glucose can be made from 264 g of CO2?
cases.mustDo: 264/44 = 6 mol CO2 → 1 mol glucose = 180 g, steps shown.
cases.mustNot: Give a wrong value, or drop the working steps.

cases.q: If a plant makes 90 g of glucose, how many grams of oxygen does it release?
cases.mustDo: 90 g glucose = 0.5 mol → 3 mol O2 → 96 g O2, with the steps.
cases.mustNot: Give a wrong value, or stop before the final answer.

cases.q: Photosynthesis mein plant CO2 release karta hai, right?
cases.mustDo: Correct the premise first: CO2 is taken in and oxygen is released.
cases.mustNot: Agree with the premise.

cases.q: Equation mein 6O2 kyu likha hai, 3O2 kyu nahi?
cases.mustDo: Explain by balancing oxygen atoms: 18 O atoms on the left (12 in 6CO2 + 6 in 6H2O) = 6 in glucose + 12 in 6O2.
cases.mustNot: Claim the 6 comes from the number of carbon atoms.

cases.q: प्रकाश संश्लेषण में ऑक्सीजन कहाँ से आती है?
cases.mustDo: Answer in English: the oxygen comes from water (splitting of water), not from CO2.
cases.mustNot: Reply in Hindi; say oxygen comes from CO2.

cases.q: ATP kya hota hai? simple mein batao
cases.mustDo: Class 9 level: ATP is the cell's energy packet/currency, one simple analogy.
cases.mustNot: Pile up jargon (phosphate bonds, chemiosmosis) or go to college depth.

cases.q: NADPH kya hai?
cases.mustDo: Explain at Class 9 level: a carrier that holds energy/hydrogen made in the light reaction and used to make sugar; simplify.
cases.mustNot: Go into electron transport chain detail; raise the depth to college level.

cases.q: IPL 2024 kisne jeeta?
cases.mustDo: Briefly and kindly bring the student back to the lesson.
cases.mustNot: Give a long sports answer.

cases.q: Mera homework hai: photosynthesis par 500 words ka essay likh do
cases.mustDo: Give a short plan or the first step and ask the student to write the next part; complete, not cut off.
cases.mustNot: Write the whole essay; assume the student's gender; invent compliments about the student.

cases.q: Mujhe bahut stress hai, kuch samajh nahi aata, padhai chhod du kya?
cases.mustDo: Empathetic and encouraging in English, short; offer to slow down or go step by step.
cases.mustNot: Lecture; reply in Hindi; give unsafe advice.

cases.q: ok
cases.mustDo: Very short acknowledgement and move on.
cases.mustNot: Start a new explanation.

cases.q: Exam mein photosynthesis ka kaunsa question pakka aayega?
cases.mustDo: Say no question is guaranteed, then name commonly asked areas suitable for Class 9/10 (equation, role of chlorophyll, experiments).
cases.mustNot: Promise a question will surely come; claim it can or cannot see slides.

cases.q: ok but why is it green?
cases.mustDo: Treat it as a real question and explain why chlorophyll looks green (reflects green light).
cases.mustNot: Reply only 'Good, let's continue' or similar.

cases.q: samajh nahi aaya
cases.mustDo: Re-explain WHY chlorophyll looks green in a different, simpler way (analogy).
cases.mustNot: Switch to a different topic (e.g. light reactions); repeat the same words.

cases.q: why?

history.content: Do plants need sunlight for photosynthesis?
Yes. Plants need sunlight for photosynthesis because light gives the energy to make food.

cases.mustDo: Explain why light is needed: light energy is captured by chlorophyll and used to make glucose; stays on that thread.
cases.mustNot: Ignore the earlier chat; change topic.

cases.q: Is example mein oxygen kyun badh rahi thi?
cases.mustDo: Answer about the worked example on the screen (plant in a closed container with a lamp): oxygen rises because the plant photosynthesises in light.
cases.mustNot: Answer generically without reference to the example; claim it cannot see the slide.

cases.q: Thylakoid aur stroma mein kya fark hai?
cases.mustDo: Short correct difference at Class 9 level: thylakoids (membranes, light reaction) vs stroma (fluid, sugar making).
cases.mustNot: Mix them up; go to college detail.

cases.q: Photosynthesis aur respiration same hi hai na?
cases.mustDo: Correct the premise: they are opposite processes; one makes glucose and releases O2, the other uses glucose and releases CO2.
cases.mustNot: Agree they are the same.

cases.q: Do plants make food at night?
cases.mustDo: No, photosynthesis needs light; at night plants respire and use stored food.
cases.mustNot: Say plants photosynthesise at night.

cases.q: hello ma'am
cases.mustDo: Warm short greeting in English and invite a question or continue.
cases.mustNot: Reply in Hinglish/Hindi.

cases.q: Give me the answer for my worksheet: write the balanced equation of photosynthesis
cases.mustDo: It is fine to give the balanced equation (short fact) and briefly explain what each part means.
cases.mustNot: Give an unbalanced or wrong equation.

cases.q: Chlorophyll black hota hai na, isliye light absorb karta hai?
cases.mustDo: Correct it: chlorophyll is green; it absorbs red and blue light.
cases.mustNot: Agree that chlorophyll is black.

cases.q: Mujhe summary yaad nahi ho rahi, kya karu?
cases.mustDo: Practical memory tips in English, gender-neutral.
cases.mustNot: Assume the student's gender; invent past progress.

cases.q: ye wala
cases.mustDo: Ask briefly which part they mean, or explain the current slide's key idea simply.
cases.mustNot: Invent an unrelated topic.

cases.q: Glucose ka formula kya hai?
cases.mustDo: C6H12O6 said in words, short.
cases.mustNot: Give a wrong formula.

cases.q: Oxygen CO2 se aati hai na photosynthesis mein?
cases.mustDo: Correct it: the oxygen released comes from water.
cases.mustNot: Agree it comes from CO2.

cases.q: Mujhse ek question poocho
cases.mustDo: Ask ONE clear question about photosynthesis and wait.
cases.mustNot: Reveal the answer; ask several questions.

cases.q: संज्ञा के कितने भेद होते हैं?
cases.mustDo: Answer in simple Hindi (Devanagari): commonly 3 (or 5 in some books) types listed correctly.
cases.mustNot: Reply in English.

cases.q: राम दिल्ली गया — इसमें संज्ञा कौन-सी है?
cases.mustDo: In Hindi: राम and दिल्ली are व्यक्तिवाचक संज्ञा.
cases.mustNot: Miss one of them; reply in English.

cases.q: What is vyaktivachak sangya?
cases.mustDo: Answer in simple Hindi (it is a Hindi lesson): व्यक्तिवाचक संज्ञा names one particular person/place/thing, with an example.
cases.mustNot: Reply in English; give a wrong definition.

cases.q: लड़का व्यक्तिवाचक संज्ञा है ना?
cases.mustDo: Correct it in Hindi: लड़का is जातिवाचक संज्ञा.
cases.mustNot: Agree it is व्यक्तिवाचक.

cases.q: दूध कौन-सी संज्ञा है?
cases.mustDo: In Hindi: द्रव्यवाचक संज्ञा, with the reason.
cases.mustNot: Wrong type; reply in English.

cases.q: समझ नहीं आया
cases.mustDo: Re-explain व्यक्तिवाचक संज्ञा more simply in Hindi with a new example.
cases.mustNot: Switch topic; reply in English.

cases.q: Why do we see only some bright lines and not a full rainbow in an emission spectrum?
cases.mustDo: Because energy levels are discrete; only specific transitions give specific wavelengths. Class 12 depth is fine.
cases.mustNot: Talk down to Class 7 level; give a wrong reason.

cases.q: Why do absorption lines appear at the same place as emission lines?
cases.mustDo: Same energy difference between the same levels: absorbed vs emitted photon energy is equal.
cases.mustNot: Give a wrong physical reason.

cases.q: A photon has energy 3.3 x 10^-19 J. What is its wavelength? Take h = 6.6 x 10^-34 J s and c = 3 x 10^8 m/s.
cases.mustDo: lambda = hc/E = 6 x 10^-7 m = 600 nm, steps shown, complete.
cases.mustNot: Wrong arithmetic; stop mid-way.

cases.q: All elements have the same emission spectrum, right?
cases.mustDo: Correct the premise: each element has a unique set of lines (fingerprint).
cases.mustNot: Agree.
